title: feat: sweep briefs come from the contract; the meter holds
headline: A sweep's briefs are written from its cleared contract, each reviewer's report is checked for shape, and the findings are counted from the reports. The call cap and token ceiling now stop a reviewer in time, the cache trip counts only expired cache, and install keeps files it used to lose.
alignment: v1.37.0 is step T6 of the v2.0 plan, one checked hand-back shape for every sweep report, with the carry-overs of builds 10 and 10-fix closed in the same release.

items.text: A cleared sweep contract writes each role's brief beside it: the rules block by line range, the sweep, cap and ceiling lines, the role's diff, a scratch folder of its own and the report shape.
A reviewer's hand-back is checked once for its report shape (a role line, one five-field line per finding or No findings, and what it did not check); the second try goes through.
A sweep's outcome counts the findings from the reviewers' reports, writes a ledger beside the contract, and refuses a typed count that differs.
The release check can read a verify's result file, and passes only when one number it recorded was run again and matched.
The call-cap hook stops a reviewer while the refused call and the report still fit under its cap and ceiling, counts only the calls before this one, and reserves for a growing context.

The cache re-write trip counts only a call that read back less than the context before it after a gap of 5 minutes or more, the time the cache lives; a large batch of new results or a trimmed context is no re-write.

A kit script followed by another command (`&& ls`, `; git status`, `; Get-ChildItem`) is no longer held as a write to a protected file; a later command that reuses its path (`$_`, `-OutVariable`, a script block) still is.
install user names the guard record of a project folder that no longer exists, and `kit.mjs forget <folder>` removes it once the folder is gone; install never deletes a record itself.
Status and session start name a newer release on GitHub, and a file kept from an unreleased build with the step that clears it; the install user fix line quotes the kit folder.
Install keeps a memory file the owner's MEMORY.md still links, keeps a file the kit renamed by case alone, and never removes a file outside its folder.
The release check lists the remote's tags only at a GitHub https address and from outside the kit folder, so no program the kit folder's git config names can run.
The guard reads a command's braces as bash does, nested lists, signed ranges, quotes and stray braces included, in one bounded pass, so a brace list cannot hide which kit project a command names.
A refused yes or resume says when the owner's Yes named the act without backticks, and `approve.mjs --tap "<act>"` checks a Yes before the owner is handed a command, without using it.
The read-only unit review in a team build runs at high effort, not xhigh (the owner, 2026-11-16: twice the cost found under a quarter more).
The push bound names opening the feature branch's PR in its own definition, and an answer about pushing or a PR names both acts and the four limits.

verification: Each fix has a test that fails on 1.36.1 and passes here.
Replayed on a real 1.36.0 reviewer's call sizes, the hook stops it where the refused call and the report land under its ceiling.
Recall on the reworded rules: median 13 of 14 against the 1.36.1 baseline of 13, scored blind.

decisions.decision: The rules block is read by line range, not moved to a file of its own
decisions.why: Moving it would make every kit project move its filled block by hand; the brief's line range gives the same smaller read with no change to any project.

decisions.decision: The release check lists tags, it does not fetch
decisions.why: A fetch inside the kit folder ran a program its git config named (the push security review); a listing of a GitHub https address reads no repo config and writes nothing.

decisions.decision: A record of a missing project folder is named, never removed by install
decisions.why: A folder on an unplugged drive is missing too; removing its record lost the owner's accept history (the sweep). Removal is a separate forget step, run once the folder is truly gone.

dimensions.name: Privacy
dimensions.result: Records and memory stay on the machine; install names a missing record and never removes one

dimensions.name: Supply chain
dimensions.result: The release listing reads only a GitHub https address, with no git config, fixed

dimensions.name: Code security
dimensions.result: Protected writes beside a kit script, brace reading, report forging, all fixed

dimensions.name: Gaps, scaling, test value
dimensions.result: The meter margins, record loss, pins and test gaps, all fixed

fixed: A later command could reuse an exempt kit script's protected path (`$_`, `-OutVariable`, a script block). Fixed in 5efed38 and 5085f64.
Install deleted the record, shims and accept history of a project folder it could not reach. Fixed in e0aee64.
A link inside a project let install remove a file outside it. Fixed in 3fa5876.
A refused report still counted, and one unreadable report switched off the count check for every role. Fixed in a96c323.
Six test lines pinned whole sentences, and the release listing test passed on the old kit. Fixed in a96c323 and 3f4c0dd.

upgrading: Run `install user` first, then `install project` in each project. A sweep cleared on 1.37.0 writes its briefs beside its contract: pass each as written.
limits: The report shape and the ledger hold only where the canary runs (a project with a confirmation phrase); a sweep in the kit source counts findings by hand as before.
